source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is sunlight exposure recommended in osteomalacia?
questions.rationale: UV light converts 7-dehydrocholesterol in skin into vitamin D.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteomalacia (PDF p. 465)
questions.quote: ultraviolet radiation transforms a cholesterol substance

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client reports his hat no longer fits and has bowed legs. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Paget's: rapid bone turnover, skull enlargement, bowing, high alkaline phosphatase.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Paget's Disease (PDF p. 465)
questions.quote: Patient may report that a hat no longer fits

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which lab finding is typical of Paget's disease?
questions.rationale: Elevated alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Paget's Diagnostics (PDF p. 465)
questions.quote: Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most common cause of osteomyelitis is:
questions.rationale: S. aureus is most common.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteomyelitis (PDF p. 466)
questions.quote: Staphylococcus aureus. (most common)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is osteomyelitis difficult to eradicate?
questions.rationale: Avascular infected bone limits immune response and antibiotic penetration.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteomyelitis Facts (PDF p. 466)
questions.quote: the infected bone is avascular

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: IV antibiotic therapy for osteomyelitis usually continues for:
questions.rationale: IV antibiotics for 3–6 weeks; chronic cases may need debridement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteomyelitis Therapy (PDF p. 466)
questions.quote: IV antibiotic therapy continues for 3 to 6 weeks

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Bilateral, symmetric joint swelling with prolonged morning stiffness suggests:
questions.rationale: RA is systemic and symmetric with synovial inflammation and pannus.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Rheumatoid Arthritis (PDF p. 467)
questions.quote: Bilateral and symmetric stiffness, tenderness, swelling

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Rheumatoid arthritis is best described as:
questions.rationale: RA is a faulty immune response attacking synovium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Rheumatoid Arthritis (PDF p. 467)
questions.quote: In RA, the autoimmune reaction primarily occurs in the synovial tissue.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is the initial analgesic for osteoarthritis?
questions.rationale: Acetaminophen first, then NSAIDs, COX-2 inhibitors, intra-articular steroids.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteoarthritis (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Initial analgesic therapy is acetaminophen

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which teaching best reduces knee pain in an obese client with osteoarthritis?
questions.rationale: Weight loss and moderate exercise reduce joint stress and disability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Osteoarthritis (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Weight reduction

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Sudden excruciating pain and redness of the big toe suggests:
questions.rationale: Podagra: urate crystal deposition in the great toe.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gout (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: most commonly the big toe (podagra)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug is used for an acute gout attack?
questions.rationale: Colchicine and NSAIDs for acute attacks; allopurinol for chronic gout.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gout Treatment (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Acute treatment is managed with colchicine

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food should a client with gout limit?
questions.rationale: High-purine foods: organ meats, sardines, anchovies, mackerel; also avoid alcohol.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gout Nursing (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Organ meals

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with gout should drink about how much fluid daily?
questions.rationale: About 3 L/day prevents uric acid crystallization in the kidneys.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Gout Nursing (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Have the patient drink 3 liters of fluid per day

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding during school screening suggests scoliosis?
questions.rationale: Scoliosis: uneven shoulders and hips, asymmetric rib cage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Scoliosis (PDF p. 469)
questions.quote: Uneven hip and shoulder levels

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After spinal fusion for scoliosis, the child is repositioned by:
questions.rationale: Log roll every 2 hours to protect the spine and prevent pressure sores.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Scoliosis Nursing (PDF p. 469)
questions.quote: Use log rolling to reposition the child every 2 hours

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head in a young child is:
questions.rationale: LCP: decreased blood supply to the femoral head; self-limiting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Legg-Calvé-Perthes (PDF p. 469)
questions.quote: characterized by necrosis of the femoral head

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A fracture where bone breaks through the skin is:
questions.rationale: Open fractures break the skin; greenstick is incomplete; comminuted has fragments.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fractures (PDF p. 470)
questions.quote: An open fracture (compound, or complex, fracture)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When splinting a suspected fracture, the nurse should immobilize:
questions.rationale: Immobilize joints proximal and distal to prevent fragment movement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fracture Emergency (PDF p. 470)
questions.quote: Joints proximal and distal to the fracture must be immobilized

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most common primary malignant bone tumor in adolescents is:
questions.rationale: Osteosarcoma affects rapidly growing bones (distal femur, proximal tibia).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Malignant Bone Tumors (PDF p. 470)
questions.quote: Osteosarcoma (ie, osteogenic sarcoma) is the most common

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with bone metastases from breast cancer becomes lethargic and constipated. The nurse checks:
questions.rationale: Bone breakdown causes hypercalcemia; treat with saline hydration and bisphosphonates.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Metastatic Bone Disease (PDF p. 471)
questions.quote: Hypercalcemia results from breakdown of bone
